Asia's largest drone exhibition and conference, ‘DSK 2025 (Drone Show Korea),’ will be held from February 26 to 28 for three days at BEXCO in Busan.

This year marks the 10th anniversary of ‘Drone Show Korea,’ and the event has been rebranded as ‘DSK.’ DSK 2025 will feature the largest exhibition to date, with 15 countries (including Korea), 1,130 booths of 306 companies (66 overseas companies), and 26,508㎡ of exhibition space.
Additionally, there will be a conference with 44 speakers and chairs from 9 countries and various experiential events.

The event will also welcome foreign ambassadors to Korea, military generals, police officers, government officials, and representatives from international organizations from 20 countries, who will participate as buyers to engage in various business exchanges with domestic companies.

The Aerospace Pavilion, where KASA participates for the first time this year, will present a new business model for DSK 2025, expanding from drones to space and aviation, featuring research institutes, universities, startups, and small and medium-sized enterprises.

Notably, the pavilion will showcase: Exhibits representing the space and aviation industries, such as Nuri rocket and stratospheric drones; Products from the "Space Pioneer Project," a key domestic technology localization project for launch vehicles and satellites (such as GNSS receivers for geostationary satellites); Advanced technologies developed by private aerospace companies, all gathered in one place.
The conference will be held over two days, from February 26 to February 27.

On the morning of Day 1, the keynote speakers will be Clinton Heimann, Deputy Director General Spatial Planning and Land Use Management of the South African Department of Land Reform and Rural Development, and Lee Bo-hyeong, Senior Researcher at the Korea Aerospace Research Institute (and the first Commander of the Drone Operations Command), who will provide insights into the latest trends in the global drone industry and the future development direction of aviation and mobility sectors.

On the afternoon of Day 1, the World Bank, Drone Life (a U.S. drone industry media outlet), and UbiFi (the first Korean drone company to reach $10 million in exports) will discuss global drone market trends and strategies for Korean drone companies’ international expansion.

On Day 2, the conference will be divided into two tracks covering topics such as drone commercialization, laws and policies, technology, global market entry cases, AI, future driving force, and sustainable aviation.

Meanwhile, the Drone Entertainment Zone (including activities like drone race on water and e-drone racing) will be held from February 26 to 28, from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM in Hall 3 of the exhibition center.

Notably, on the evening of February 26 at 7:00 PM (approximately 10 minutes), a 600-drone show will take place in the outdoor area of BEXCO under the theme "Connecting and Innovating the Future." The viewing area will be located near the flagpole at the outdoor exhibition hall of BEXCO.

Vice Administrator of KASA, Kyungwon Rho, stated, "Drones are being utilized in various fields, such as space exploration, defense, logistics, agriculture, and disaster response." He emphasized the high potential of drone applications in our society and further stated, "KASA will spare no effort in providing institutional support and R&D investments to ensure that Korea’s drone industry gains global competitiveness," sharing his vision for the drone industry.
